q: In the PL Number of a stores item, the first two digits indicate:

options.A: The group to which the item belongs
options.B: The depot holding the item
options.C: The year of first purchase of the item
options.D: The supplier of the item

e: In the 8-digit PL Number, the first two digits indicate the group to which the item belongs, placing it within the uniform stores classification.

q:
Codification of stores items through PL numbers serves to:
1. Identify each item uniquely in all depots
2. Facilitate computerised inventory control, e.g. through iMMS
3. Prevent the same item being stocked under different names

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 1 and 2 only
options.C: 2 and 3 only
options.D: 1, 2 and 3

e: PL codification serves all three purposes: it identifies each item uniquely in all depots, facilitates computerised inventory control through iMMS, and prevents the same item being stocked under different names.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The re-order level of an item is fixed at the consumption during the lead time plus the safety (buffer) stock.
2. The safety (buffer) stock is meant to absorb variations in consumption and in lead time.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the re-order level equals lead-time consumption plus safety stock, and the safety (buffer) stock exists precisely to absorb variations in consumption and lead time.

q: The 'danger level' of a stock item is the level:

options.A: Above the maximum level fixed for the item
options.B: Below the minimum level, at which emergency action to replenish the stock must be taken
options.C: At which the item is declared obsolete
options.D: Equal to the average annual consumption of the item

e: The danger level lies below the minimum level; when stock falls to it, emergency action must be taken to replenish the stock before it runs out.

q: The maximum stock level of an item is computed as:

options.A: Re-order level + Re-order quantity - (Minimum consumption x Minimum lead time)
options.B: Re-order level + Average consumption
options.C: Safety stock + Lead time
options.D: Annual consumption divided by 12

e: Maximum level = Re-order level + Re-order quantity - (Minimum consumption x Minimum lead time). This caps the stock so it does not exceed the highest quantity likely to be held.

q: Value Analysis, as applied to stores items, is a technique for:

options.A: Assessing the resale value of scrap
options.B: Verifying the physical stock held in depots
options.C: Fixing the sale price of surplus stores
options.D: Reducing the cost of an item by examining the function it performs and eliminating unnecessary cost, without impairing its quality or utility

e: Value Analysis reduces the cost of an item by examining the function it performs and eliminating unnecessary cost, without impairing its quality, reliability or utility.

q: Railway stores accounts follow the perpetual inventory system, which means:

options.A: Stock is counted only once at the end of the year and no records are kept during the year
options.B: Bin cards are dispensed with altogether
options.C: No priced ledger is maintained for stores
options.D: Book balances of every item are continuously maintained and are physically verified in rotation

e: Under the perpetual inventory system, book balances of every item are continuously maintained (through bin cards and priced ledgers) and are physically verified in rotation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Surplus stores are serviceable stores which are not required by the depot holding them.
2. Obsolete stores are stores which can no longer be put to use because of a change in design or technology.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: surplus stores are serviceable but not required by the holding depot, while obsolete stores cannot be used at all due to change in design or technology.

q: Returnable stores, such as tools and plant, are:

options.A: Consumed as soon as they are issued
options.B: Issued for use against acknowledgement and required to be returned to stores after use
options.C: Sold to the staff after use
options.D: Written off from the books at the time of issue

e: Returnable stores like tools and plant are issued for use against acknowledgement and must be returned to stores after use; they are not consumed on issue.

q: At the divisional level, the stores organisation of a zonal railway is headed by the:

options.A: Senior Divisional Materials Manager
options.B: Senior Divisional Accounts Officer
options.C: Controller of Stores
options.D: Chief Materials Manager of the workshop

e: At the divisional level, the stores organisation of a zonal railway is headed by the Senior Divisional Materials Manager (Sr.DMM).

q: When the charge of a stores depot changes hands, the incoming custodian:

options.A: Takes over on the basis of book balances without any check
options.B: Refuses charge until the annual stock verification is completed
options.C: Takes over only the A-category items
options.D: Takes over the stores after verification of balances, and discrepancies, if any, are brought on record

e: On change of charge, the incoming custodian takes over stores after verification of balances, and any discrepancies found are brought on record before he accepts charge.

q: Stores held in the custody of user departments (outside the stores depots) are physically verified by:

options.A: The Accounts stock verifiers in all cases
options.B: The depot storekeeper
options.C: Officers of the department holding the stores
options.D: The Travelling Inspector of Stores Accounts

e: Stores held by user departments outside the depots are physically verified by officers of the department holding them, since those stores are in that department's custody.

q: Stock verification in a stores depot is so arranged that:

options.A: All items are verified on one single day of the year
options.B: Every item is physically verified at least once in a year
options.C: Only items costing above Rs 1 lakh are verified
options.D: Verification is carried out once in five years

e: Stock verification is arranged in rotation so that every item in a depot is physically verified at least once in a year.

q: Losses of stores, e.g. deficiencies found in stock verification, are written off:

options.A: By the competent authority at the appropriate level, according to the value of the loss, under the delegation of powers
options.B: By the storekeeper maintaining the bin card
options.C: Only by the Railway Board, whatever the amount involved
options.D: Automatically at the close of the financial year

e: Losses of stores are written off by the competent authority at the appropriate level, according to the value of the loss, under the delegation of powers - not by the storekeeper.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A stores loss can be written off straightaway, without any enquiry, as soon as it is noticed.
2. Before a stores loss is written off, the responsibility for it is investigated and fixed, and recovery is made from the official at fault where negligence is established.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: a loss cannot be written off straightaway without enquiry. Statement 2 is true: responsibility is investigated and fixed first, with recovery from the official at fault where negligence is established.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Emergency purchase powers are meant for meeting genuine and unforeseen urgency, and not for bypassing normal tendering.
2. Such purchases are subject to monetary ceilings in the delegation of powers and require the urgency to be recorded/certified by the competent authority.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: emergency purchase powers are only for genuine, unforeseen urgency, are subject to monetary ceilings, and require the urgency to be recorded/certified by the competent authority.

q: Delivery of scrap sold through e-auction is allowed to the purchaser:

options.A: As soon as the auction is knocked down, before any payment
options.B: On payment of earnest money alone
options.C: In instalments, as and when the purchaser chooses to pay
options.D: Only after the full sale value has been paid by him

e: Scrap sold through e-auction is delivered to the purchaser only after he has paid the full sale value; delivery before full payment is not permitted.

q: If a purchaser of scrap fails to lift the material within the stipulated delivery period:

options.A: Ground rent is charged for the period of delay in lifting
options.B: The Railway delivers the material free of cost to his premises
options.C: The entire sale value is refunded to him
options.D: No action lies against the purchaser

e: If a scrap purchaser fails to lift the material within the stipulated delivery period, ground rent is charged to him for the period of the delay in lifting.

q: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, a 'Class-II local supplier' is one whose local content is:

options.A: Less than 10%
options.B: At least 10% but less than 20%
options.C: At least 20% but less than 50%

e: Under the Make in India Order, a Class-II local supplier is one whose local content is at least 20% but less than 50%.

q: Through the user depot module of iMMS, a consuming department can:

options.A: Pass suppliers' bills for payment
options.B: Conduct e-auctions of scrap
options.C: Fix the AAC of A-category items
options.D: View the stock position of items in depots and raise its demands online

e: Through the user depot module of iMMS, a consuming department can view the stock position of items in depots and raise its demands (indents) online.

q: A railway stores depot is organised into:

options.A: Wards and sections, each ward holding a distinct group of stores in the custody of a storekeeper
options.B: A single common godown in which all items are mixed together without separate custody
options.C: A separate depot for every individual item of stores
options.D: Offices only, the stores being kept with the consuming departments

e: A stores depot is organised into wards and sections, each ward holding a distinct group of stores in the custody of a storekeeper, ensuring clear responsibility for each group.

q: The officer in charge of a stores depot is the:

options.A: Controller of Stores
options.B: Depot Materials Superintendent (DMS)
options.C: Senior Divisional Materials Manager
options.D: Principal Financial Adviser

e: The officer in charge of a stores depot is the Depot Materials Superintendent (DMS), who is responsible for the depot's stores and staff.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Custody (numerical) accounts of stores record quantities only and are maintained by the stock holder (custodian).
2. Priced accounts of stores record quantities as well as values and are maintained by the Accounts Department.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: custody (numerical) accounts record quantities only and are kept by the stock holder, while priced accounts record quantities and values and are kept by the Accounts Department.

q: The priced accounts of stores differ from the custody accounts in that the priced accounts:

options.A: Are maintained by the depot storekeeper at the bins
options.B: Record quantities only, without any value
options.C: Are dispensed with when a priced ledger is maintained
options.D: Record both quantities and values and are maintained by the Accounts Department, while custody accounts record quantities only and are maintained by the stock holder

e: Priced accounts differ from custody accounts in recording both quantities and values; they are maintained by the Accounts Department, whereas custody accounts show quantities only and are kept by the stock holder.

q: Material received at a stores depot but awaiting inspection is taken into the priced stock accounts:

options.A: Immediately on its arrival at the depot gate
options.B: Only after it has been inspected and accepted and a receipt note issued
options.C: As soon as it is issued to a consuming department
options.D: Only at the end of the financial year

e: Material awaiting inspection enters the priced stock accounts only after it has been inspected, accepted and a receipt note issued for it.

q: Where material received at a depot is found short or damaged at the time of receipt:

options.A: It is accepted silently and the loss is ignored
options.B: The shortage is always borne personally by the storekeeper without any record
options.C: The shortage/damage is recorded on the receipt documents and a claim is preferred on the supplier or the carrier, as the case may be
options.D: The amount is deducted from the next bill of the firm without any record

e: Shortage or damage found at receipt is recorded on the receipt documents and a claim is preferred on the supplier or the carrier, as the case may be - it is never ignored.

q: Custody accounts and priced accounts of stores are maintained as two independent sets of records so that:

options.A: One of them can be dispensed with in alternate years
options.B: The priced accounts can simply replace the custody accounts
options.C: The depot staff need not maintain any quantity record
options.D: Each set serves as a check on the other and the two can be agreed with each other

e: Custody and priced accounts are kept as two independent sets so that each serves as a check on the other and the two can be agreed with each other.

q: Stores despatched by one depot to another depot under a transfer remain accounted for in the books of the despatching depot:

options.A: Only until the wagon leaves the depot siding
options.B: Until their receipt is acknowledged by the receiving depot
options.C: Until the end of the month of despatch, in all cases
options.D: They are removed from all accounts the moment they are despatched

e: Stores despatched to another depot under transfer remain on the books of the despatching depot until the receiving depot acknowledges their receipt.

q: Stores returned to a depot by a consuming department or work are, after examination, classified as:

options.A: Scrap only, whatever their condition
options.B: Serviceable only, whatever their condition
options.C: Re-usable (serviceable), repairable, or scrap, according to their condition
options.D: Imported or indigenous, according to their source

e: Returned stores are examined and classified according to their condition as re-usable (serviceable), repairable, or scrap.

q: Serviceable (re-usable) stores returned to a depot are taken back into stock:

options.A: At the value assessed for the returned material, the returning work/department being given credit at that value
options.B: Always at the price at which they were originally purchased, ignoring their present condition
options.C: At the current market price of new material
options.D: Without giving any credit to the returning work or department

e: Serviceable stores returned to a depot are taken back into stock at the assessed value of the returned material, and the returning work/department is given credit at that assessed value.

q: Stores returned to a depot as 'repairable' are those which:

options.A: Are fit for immediate issue without any attention
options.B: Can only be thrown away as refuse
options.C: Are sold to the staff at the depot itself
options.D: Can be made serviceable again after repair, e.g. in a workshop, and are taken back into stock after repair

e: 'Repairable' returned stores are those that can be made serviceable again after repair, e.g. in a workshop; they are taken back into stock after being repaired.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Returned stores are always taken into stock at the price at which they were originally issued.
2. The work or department returning serviceable stores to a depot is given credit at the assessed value of the stores returned.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: returned stores are not taken back at the original issue price. Statement 2 is true: the returning work/department gets credit at the assessed value of the stores returned.

q: Returned stores which are classified as scrap are:

options.A: Returned to the original supplier free of cost
options.B: Kept in the depot indefinitely without any entry
options.C: Issued to the staff for personal use
options.D: Condemned after survey and disposed of by sale as scrap

e: Returned stores classified as scrap are condemned after survey and disposed of by sale as scrap, like other scrap arising in the depot.

q: Stores issued or sold to outside parties and other Government departments are priced at:

options.A: The current market price on the day of issue
options.B: The book value plus the prescribed departmental charges
options.C: Half the book value
options.D: No charge is made, issues to outsiders being free

e: Stores issued or sold to outside parties and other Government departments are priced at book value plus the prescribed departmental charges, covering incidental and overhead costs.

q: Earnest money deposited by bidders who remain unsuccessful in an e-auction of scrap is:

options.A: Refunded to them after finalisation of the auction
options.B: Forfeited to the Railway in all cases
options.C: Adjusted compulsorily against their future purchases
options.D: Credited to the personal account of the depot officer

e: Earnest money of bidders who remain unsuccessful in a scrap e-auction is refunded to them after finalisation of the auction; only the successful bidder's deposit is retained.

q: In the e-auction of scrap, the material is sold:

options.A: To the bidder who quotes the lowest rate
options.B: To the first bidder who registers on the portal
options.C: By draw of lots among the registered bidders
options.D: Lot-wise, to the highest bidder for each lot, subject to acceptance of the bid

e: In scrap e-auction, material is sold lot-wise to the highest bidder for each lot, subject to acceptance of the bid by the competent authority.

q: The highest bid received in an e-auction of scrap results in a concluded sale:

options.A: The moment the highest bid is placed, no approval being necessary
options.B: Only after the bid is accepted by the competent authority
options.C: As soon as any depot clerk notes the bid
options.D: Only after approval of the Railway Board in every case

e: The highest bid does not by itself conclude the sale; the sale is concluded only after the bid is accepted by the competent authority.

q: Where a purchaser of scrap defaults in paying the sale value or lifting the material as per the sale conditions:

options.A: No action lies against him
options.B: The delivery period is extended indefinitely without any charge
options.C: The earnest money/sale deposit paid by him is liable to be forfeited and the lot may be re-auctioned, as per the sale conditions
options.D: The Railway is required to pay him compensation

e: On a scrap purchaser's default in payment or lifting, his earnest money/sale deposit is liable to be forfeited and the lot may be re-auctioned, as per the sale conditions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Scrap offered for sale by e-auction is described in an auction catalogue divided into lots bearing lot numbers.
2. Only bidders registered for the auction, who have deposited the prescribed earnest money, can participate in the bidding.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: scrap is offered in an auction catalogue divided into numbered lots, and only registered bidders who have deposited the prescribed earnest money can bid.

q: The Stores Miscellaneous Suspense head is operated to accommodate:

options.A: The value of stores issued, e.g. to other railways, departments or firms, pending final adjustment or recovery
options.B: Salary of stores staff pending allotment of funds
options.C: Freight charges on coaching traffic
options.D: Deposits received from tenderers for works contracts

e: Stores Miscellaneous Suspense is operated to accommodate the value of stores issued, e.g. to other railways, departments or firms, pending final adjustment or recovery.

q: Balances outstanding under the stores suspense heads are:

options.A: Never reviewed once they are booked
options.B: Reviewed periodically and cleared by linking them with the corresponding bills and adjustments
options.C: Written off automatically at the end of every year without any linking
options.D: Transferred to the Capital account at the end of the year

e: Balances under the stores suspense heads are reviewed periodically and cleared by linking them with the corresponding bills and adjustments; they are not left outstanding indefinitely.

q: The net balance of the Stock Adjustment Account accumulated during a year is finally cleared:

options.A: By carrying it forward indefinitely from year to year
options.B: By transfer to the Purchase Suspense Account
options.C: By adjustment against the earnings of coaching traffic
options.D: At the close of the year, under the sanction of the competent authority

e: The net balance of the Stock Adjustment Account accumulated during a year is finally cleared at the close of the year, under the sanction of the competent authority.

q: The Stock Adjustment Account is distinguished from the Purchase Suspense Account in that the Stock Adjustment Account:

options.A: Records bills paid for material not received
options.B: Records sale value deposited by purchasers of scrap
options.C: Adjusts differences in the quantity and value of stock, whereas Purchase Suspense bridges the gap between payment of bills and receipt of material, and vice versa
options.D: Is maintained only by the Traffic Accounts office

e: The Stock Adjustment Account adjusts differences in quantity and value of stock, whereas Purchase Suspense bridges the gap between payment of bills and receipt of material (and vice versa).

q: When the book (issue) rate of a stores item is revised, the difference in the value of the stock in hand consequent on the revision is adjusted through the:

options.A: Stock Adjustment Account
options.B: Purchase Suspense Account
options.C: No account - such differences are ignored
options.D: Personal account of the storekeeper

e: When the book (issue) rate of an item is revised, the resulting difference in the value of stock in hand is adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: The balances in the custody (bin) accounts and the priced accounts of stores are:

options.A: Never compared with each other
options.B: Agreed with each other periodically, differences being investigated before they are adjusted
options.C: Agreed by altering the priced ledger to match the bin card without any enquiry
options.D: Compared only once in ten years

e: Balances in the custody (bin) accounts and the priced accounts are agreed with each other periodically, and differences are investigated before being adjusted - never written straight into the ledger.

q: The half-yearly Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts is:

options.A: A statement prepared half-yearly showing the balances of stores under stock and suspense heads and proving the agreement of the priced ledger with the accounts (general) books
options.B: A statement of the attendance of stores staff for six months
options.C: A list of tenders opened during the half year
options.D: A statement of the dues recoverable from stores staff

e: The half-yearly Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts shows the balances under stock and suspense heads and proves the agreement of the priced ledger with the general (accounts) books.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts covers balances under the stock heads as well as the stores suspense heads.
2. Any disagreement between the priced ledger balances and the balances in the general books is investigated and reconciled.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts covers stock as well as suspense balances, and any disagreement between the priced ledger and the general books is investigated and reconciled.

q: Inventory carrying cost of stores is ordinarily expressed as:

options.A: A fixed amount per depot, irrespective of the stock held
options.B: A proportion (percentage) of the average value of the inventory held, per annum
options.C: A charge per item, irrespective of its value
options.D: A percentage of the salary bill of the stores department

e: Inventory carrying cost is ordinarily expressed as a percentage of the average value of inventory held, per annum, since cost elements like interest vary with the value locked up.

q: The total inventory carrying cost borne by a railway increases with:

options.A: A fall in the average stock held
options.B: A reduction in the period for which stock is held
options.C: The elimination of dead and surplus stock
options.D: The average value of stock held and the period for which it is held

e: Total carrying cost rises with the average value of stock held and the period for which it is held; reducing either reduces the carrying cost.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Dead and surplus stock adds to the inventory carrying cost without contributing to issues.
2. Reducing obsolete and surplus stock is an objective of inventory control, partly because it cuts the inventory carrying cost.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: dead and surplus stock keeps incurring carrying cost without contributing to issues, so reducing obsolete and surplus stock - an objective of inventory control - cuts that cost.

q: Buffer (safety) stock norms for A-category items are kept comparatively tight (low) mainly because:

options.A: A-category items are consumed only once in many years
options.B: A large amount of capital is locked up in every unit of A-category stock, so excess buffer is costly
options.C: A-category items are never required in an emergency
options.D: A-category items are always available off the shelf in the market

e: A-category items have very high unit value, so every extra unit of buffer locks up a large amount of capital and adds carrying cost; their safety stock is therefore kept tight.

q: The 'coverage' of a stock item means:

options.A: The quantity ordered in a single purchase order
options.B: The shelf life of the item in the depot
options.C: The validity period of the tender for the item
options.D: The period for which the stock in hand and on order (dues) will meet the consumption requirements of the item

e: Coverage means the period for which the stock in hand plus dues (quantities already on order) will meet the consumption requirements of the item.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A-category items are comparatively few in number but account for the bulk of the annual consumption value.
2. A-category items are reviewed less frequently than C-category items.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: A-category items are few in number but account for the bulk of annual consumption value. Statement 2 is wrong, as A items are reviewed more frequently, not less, because of their high value.

q: In the import of stores, a Letter of Credit (LC) is:

options.A: A letter issued by the Railway Board to the foreign supplier
options.B: A form prescribed by the Customs Department for assessment of duty
options.C: An inspection certificate issued by the inspecting authority abroad
options.D: An undertaking of a bank to pay the foreign supplier against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents

e: A Letter of Credit is an undertaking by a bank to pay the foreign supplier against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents, assuring payment for imported stores.

q: Under a Letter of Credit opened for imported stores, payment to the foreign supplier is made:

options.A: Against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents through the bank, and not on the physical receipt of the material in India
options.B: Only after the material has been received and verified in the Indian depot
options.C: In cash to the supplier's agent at the Indian port
options.D: Only after the close of the financial year in which the order was placed

e: Under a Letter of Credit, payment is released against the stipulated shipping documents routed through the bank; it does not wait for the material to physically reach and be verified in India.

q: Customs duty on imported stores is payable:

options.A: Before the consignment is cleared through Customs at the port of entry
options.B: By the foreign supplier in all cases, the Railway paying nothing
options.C: Only on stores which are later sold as scrap
options.D: After one year from the date of import, without exception

e: Customs duty on imported stores must be paid at the port of entry before the consignment is cleared through Customs.

q: The book value of imported stores taken into stock is based on their landed cost, which comprises:

options.A: The purchase price only
options.B: The purchase price plus freight only
options.C: The purchase price, freight, insurance and customs duty
options.D: The purchase price minus the customs duty paid

e: Imported stores are taken into stock at landed cost, that is, purchase price plus freight, insurance and customs duty incurred in bringing them to the depot.

q: A warranty claim on a supplier for stores found defective must be lodged:

options.A: At any time, even long after the warranty period has expired
options.B: Within the warranty period stipulated in the contract
options.C: Only at the time of payment of the final bill, whatever the date
options.D: Only after the stores have been in use for five years

e: A warranty claim is enforceable only within the warranty period stipulated in the contract; after that period expires, the supplier is no longer bound to repair or replace.

q: Where a supplier fails to replace or repair defective stores under the warranty clause:

options.A: The Railway must bear the cost of repair itself without any remedy
options.B: The claim is dropped and the defective stores are thrown away
options.C: The depot storekeeper imposes a fine on the supplier
options.D: The Railway may arrange the repair or replacement at the supplier's risk and cost and recover the amount from his dues or security deposit

e: If the supplier fails to repair or replace defective stores under warranty, the Railway may arrange it at the supplier's risk and cost and recover the amount from his dues or security deposit.

q: Liquidated damages levied on a supplier for delayed supply are ordinarily recovered from:

options.A: The supplier's bills or his security deposit with the Railway
options.B: The pay of the depot storekeeper
options.C: The purchaser of scrap in the next auction
options.D: No recovery is made; liquidated damages are always waived

e: Liquidated damages for delayed supply are recovered from the supplier's pending bills or, failing those, from his security deposit held with the Railway.

q: The performance rating of registered vendors (firms) in stores procurement is used for:

options.A: Fixing the market price of stores items
options.B: Deciding promotions of stores staff
options.C: Assessing firms on the quality of their supplies, adherence to delivery and service, and guiding their registration and consideration in tenders
options.D: Clearing imported consignments through Customs

e: Vendor performance rating assesses firms on quality of supplies, adherence to delivery and service, and is used in guiding their registration and consideration in tenders.

q: The Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is:

options.A: A portal of the Railways for auction of scrap only
options.B: An online marketplace through which Government buyers procure common-use goods and services directly from sellers listed on the portal
options.C: Only a payment gateway of a nationalised bank
options.D: An inspection agency for imported stores

e: GeM, the Government e-Marketplace, is an online portal through which Government buyers procure common-use goods and services directly from sellers listed on the portal.

q: GeM is distinguished from IREPS in that:

options.A: Both are one and the same portal
options.B: GeM is used only for sale of scrap by the Railways
options.C: IREPS is the national marketplace for common-use goods
options.D: IREPS is the Railways' own e-procurement system for tenders, stores procurement and scrap e-auction, whereas GeM is the national marketplace for common-use goods and services

e: IREPS is the Railways' own e-procurement system for tenders, stores procurement and scrap e-auction, whereas GeM is the national marketplace for common-use goods and services.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Common-use goods available on GeM can be purchased by a Government buyer directly from the sellers listed on the portal.
2. Railway-specific stores continue to be procured through tendering on IREPS.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: common-use goods on GeM can be bought directly from listed sellers, and Railway-specific stores continue to be procured through tendering on IREPS.

q: A registered firm whose performance as a vendor is persistently poor may face:

options.A: Down-gradation, suspension or cancellation of its registration
options.B: Automatic allotment of larger orders as compensation
options.C: No consequence of any kind
options.D: A fine imposed personally by the depot storekeeper

e: A registered firm whose performance is persistently poor may face down-gradation, suspension or cancellation of its registration as an approved vendor.

q:
Consider the following statements about payment of stores bills:
1. Up to 98% of the value of stores may be paid against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, before the material is actually received at destination.
2. The balance 2% is paid after the material has been received, inspected and accepted at the destination depot.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: up to 98% of the value is paid against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, and the balance 2% is paid after receipt, inspection and acceptance at the destination depot.

q:
Consider the following statements about liquidated damages (LD) in stores contracts:
1. LD for delayed supply is levied at 0.5% of the value of the stores in arrear for each week or part of a week of delay.
2. The total LD recoverable under a contract is subject to a maximum of 10% of the contract value.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: liquidated damages are levied at 0.5% of the value of the stores in arrear for each week or part of a week of delay, subject to a maximum of 10% of the contract value.

q: In the Accounts Department, the abbreviation ASV stands for:

options.A: Additional Stock Verifier
options.B: Assistant Stock Verifier
options.C: Assistant Stores Valuation Officer
options.D: Accounts Stock Validator

e: In the Accounts Department, ASV stands for Assistant Stock Verifier, who is engaged in the physical verification of stores balances.

q: The standard forms used in stores depots (receipt notes, issue notes, bin cards, stock sheets) belong to which series of Indian Railway standard forms?

options.A: S-series
options.B: E-series
options.C: A-series
options.D: G-series

e: The standard forms used in stores depots, such as receipt notes, issue notes and bin cards, belong to the S-series of Indian Railway standard forms.

q: Tools and plant issued to departments for use, which remain railway property and are accountable numerically, are borne on a register called the:

options.A: Priced Stores Ledger
options.B: Bin Card
options.C: Stores Ledger
options.D: Dead Stock Register

e: Tools and plant issued to departments for use remain railway property and are borne numerically on the Dead Stock Register.

q: Stores issued from a depot to a railway workshop for use on jobs under manufacture or repair are initially debited to:

options.A: Purchase Suspense
options.B: Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: Stock Adjustment Account
options.D: Sales Suspense

e: Stores issued to a workshop for jobs under manufacture or repair are debited to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, which collects the cost of workshop jobs.

q: In a Stores Budget, the 'debits' anticipated during the year represent:

options.A: The value of stores expected to be issued to consuming departments
options.B: The closing balance of stores expected at the end of the year
options.C: The value of stores expected to be purchased and received during the year
options.D: The earnest money expected to be collected from tenderers

e: In a Stores Budget, the 'debits' anticipated represent the value of stores expected to be purchased and received (taken into stock) during the year.

q: In stores parlance, the quantities of an item which have been ordered on suppliers but not yet received are known as:

options.A: Dues
options.B: Arrears
options.C: Balances
options.D: Credits

e: Quantities of an item ordered on suppliers but not yet received are known as dues; they are counted along with stock in hand while judging coverage.

q: Non-stock stores purchased against a specific demand are ordinarily:

options.A: Stocked in the depot for general issue to all departments
options.B: Issued directly to the indentor on receipt, without being taken into the general stock balances
options.C: Kept in a separate godown for one year before issue
options.D: Returned to the supplier after use by the indentor

e: Non-stock stores purchased against a specific demand are issued directly to the indentor on receipt, without being taken into the general stock balances.

q: To prevent deterioration and obsolescence, issues of stores from stock are ordinarily made:

options.A: At random, from any bin in the ward
options.B: From the latest stock first, keeping the old stock in reserve
options.C: On the first-in-first-out (FIFO) basis, the oldest stock being issued first
options.D: Only against cash payment by the consuming department

e: Issues are made on the first-in-first-out basis, the oldest stock being issued first, so that deterioration and obsolescence of old stock are prevented.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 30 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 3 crore. The Turnover Ratio is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance / total issues = Rs 30 lakh / Rs 3 crore = 30/300 = 0.10.

q: A depot holds 100 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 10 per unit. A fresh receipt of 100 units is taken into stock at Rs 14 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item will be:

options.A: Rs 10 per unit
options.B: Rs 14 per unit
options.C: Rs 24 per unit
options.D: Rs 12 per unit

e: Revised average rate = (100 x Rs 10 + 100 x Rs 14) / 200 units = Rs 2,400 / 200 = Rs 12 per unit.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 800 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 100 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity is:

options.A: 100 units
options.B: 200 units
options.C: 400 units
options.D: 800 units

e: EOQ = sqrt(2 x annual consumption x ordering cost / carrying cost) = sqrt(2 x 800 x 100 / 4) = sqrt(40,000) = 200 units.

q: The AAC of an item is 1,200 units. Ignoring the stock in hand and the dues, the quantity required to provide six months' coverage is:

options.A: 200 units
options.B: 2,400 units
options.C: 600 units
options.D: 1,200 units

e: Quantity for six months' coverage = AAC 1,200 units x 6/12 = 600 units.

q: Immediately after the opening of stores tenders, the purchase office prepares, for placing before the Tender Committee:

options.A: A purchase order
options.B: A receipt note
options.C: A stock sheet
options.D: A comparative statement (tabulation) of the offers received

e: After tenders are opened, a comparative statement (tabulation) of the offers received is prepared and placed before the Tender Committee for its recommendations.

q: In stores procurement, the Tender Committee examines the offers and makes recommendations; the tender is finally accepted by:

options.A: The Tender Accepting Authority competent under the schedule of powers
options.B: The lowest tenderer
options.C: The depot storekeeper
options.D: The Inspector of Stores Accounts

e: The Tender Committee only examines the offers and recommends; the tender is finally accepted by the Tender Accepting Authority competent under the schedule of powers.

q: Tenders received after the due date and time fixed for their receipt/opening are:

options.A: Opened and considered along with the other tenders
options.B: Not opened/considered
options.C: Considered only if they happen to be the lowest
options.D: Kept pending for consideration in the next tender

e: Tenders received after the due date and time fixed for receipt/opening are not opened or considered, so that fairness among tenderers is preserved.

q: Where the rates received in a tender are considered unreasonable in comparison with the last accepted rate and the prevailing market rates, the competent authority may:

options.A: Accept the highest rate received
options.B: Compel the lowest firm to supply at the estimated rate
options.C: Discharge the tender and invite a fresh tender
options.D: Divide the order equally among all the tenderers

e: Where the rates received are unreasonable against the last accepted rate and prevailing market rates, the competent authority may discharge the tender and invite a fresh tender.

q: A purchase order placed on a firm against its accepted tender:

options.A: Is only an expression of intention and binds neither party
options.B: Can be withdrawn by the firm at its will at any time
options.C: Requires a separate agreement in every case before it can bind the firm
options.D: Constitutes a concluded contract binding on the supplier to supply the stores on the terms of the order

e: A purchase order placed on a firm against its accepted tender constitutes a concluded contract, binding the supplier to supply the stores on the terms of the order.

q: An amendment to a purchase order which has financial implications, e.g. a change in rate or quantity affecting the order value, is issued:

options.A: Only with the concurrence of Finance
options.B: By the depot storekeeper on his own authority
options.C: Orally by the purchase clerk dealing with the case
options.D: Without any approval, as a routine correction

e: An amendment to a purchase order having financial implications, such as a change in rate or quantity affecting the order value, is issued only with the concurrence of Finance.

q: A purchase order is said to be 'short-closed' when:

options.A: It is closed after the full quantity has been supplied and accepted
options.B: The firm on which it was placed is blacklisted
options.C: The balance quantity remaining unsupplied is no longer required and the order is closed without insisting on supply of that balance
options.D: The delivery period of the order is extended

e: An order is short-closed when the balance quantity remaining unsupplied is no longer required and the order is closed without insisting on supply of that balance.

q: Under the IRS Conditions of Contract, a contractor:

options.A: May freely assign the contract to any other firm
options.B: Shall not assign or sublet the contract, or any part of it, without the written consent of the Railway
options.C: May sublet the whole contract without informing the Railway
options.D: May transfer the contract by merely intimating the depot

e: Under the IRS Conditions of Contract, the contractor shall not assign or sublet the contract, or any part of it, without the written consent of the Railway.

q: The 'force majeure' clause in a stores contract relieves a party from liability for failure to perform the contract when the failure is due to:

options.A: A rise in the market prices of raw materials
options.B: A shortage of funds with the party
options.C: Ordinary business risks of the trade
options.D: Events beyond its control, such as war, natural calamities or epidemics

e: The force majeure clause relieves a party from liability for failure to perform when the failure is due to events beyond its control, such as war, natural calamities or epidemics.

q: Disputes arising between the Railway and a supplier in connection with a stores contract are settled, as provided in the IRS Conditions of Contract, through:

options.A: Arbitration
options.B: A complaint to the police
options.C: The stock verification process
options.D: A reference to the Inspector of Stores Accounts

e: Disputes between the Railway and a supplier under a stores contract are settled through arbitration, as provided in the IRS Conditions of Contract.

q: An Integrity Pact, as adopted in high-value procurements, is:

options.A: A bond furnished by the successful tenderer along with the security deposit
options.B: A clause providing for levy of liquidated damages
options.C: An agreement between the purchaser and the bidders committing both sides to refrain from corrupt practices, overseen by Independent External Monitors
options.D: An undertaking by the supplier to always quote the lowest rate

e: An Integrity Pact is an agreement between the purchaser and the bidders committing both sides to refrain from corrupt practices, overseen by Independent External Monitors.

q: Under Rule 144(xi) of the General Financial Rules, a bidder from a country which shares a land border with India is eligible to participate in a tender only if the bidder is:

options.A: Registered with the local chamber of commerce of that country
options.B: Registered with the Registration Committee set up by the DPIIT
options.C: Approved by the depot officer inviting the tender
options.D: Exempted from payment of earnest money

e: Under Rule 144(xi) of the General Financial Rules, a bidder from a country sharing a land border with India is eligible only if registered with the Registration Committee set up by the DPIIT.

q: Splitting up a stores demand or an indent into smaller parts merely to bring it within the financial powers of a lower authority is:

options.A: A recommended measure of economy
options.B: Permitted at the level of the depot officer
options.C: Permitted with the approval of the storekeeper
options.D: Not permissible

e: Splitting up a demand or indent into smaller parts merely to bring it within the financial powers of a lower authority is not permissible.

q: Stores purchase contracts on Indian Railways are ordinarily placed on 'F.O.R. destination' terms, which means that:

options.A: The supplier bears the transit risk and the price covers delivery at the destination depot
options.B: The Railway collects the material from the supplier's factory at its own risk and cost
options.C: Freight is always paid separately by the consignee in every case
options.D: Inspection of the material is dispensed with altogether

e: On F.O.R. destination terms, the supplier bears the transit risk and the price covers delivery of the stores at the destination depot.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Pre-despatch inspection of stores does not deprive the consignee of the right to reject material which, on receipt, is found not to conform to the specification.
2. Rejection of material at destination must be communicated to the supplier within the period stipulated in the contract, through a rejection advice.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: pre-despatch inspection does not take away the consignee's right to reject non-conforming material on receipt, and rejection must be communicated to the supplier within the period stipulated in the contract.

q: Where a supplier fails to remove rejected material from the depot within the stipulated period, the material:

options.A: Becomes the personal property of the storekeeper
options.B: Is liable to storage/ground charges and may ultimately be disposed of at the supplier's risk, as per the conditions of contract
options.C: Is issued to the user department free of cost
options.D: Is automatically accepted into stock after the period expires

e: Rejected material not removed by the supplier within the stipulated period is liable to storage/ground charges and may ultimately be disposed of at the supplier's risk, as per the conditions of contract.

q: Before effecting a risk purchase against a defaulting supplier, the Railway is required to:

options.A: Obtain the permission of the lowest tenderer in the original tender
options.B: File a suit against the supplier in a court of law
options.C: Refund the security deposit of the supplier in full
options.D: Serve a notice on the defaulting supplier calling upon him to supply the stores, failing which the purchase will be made at his risk and cost

e: Before effecting a risk purchase, a notice must be served on the defaulting supplier calling upon him to supply the stores, failing which the purchase will be made at his risk and cost.

q: Under the price variation clause of a stores contract, the adjustment of prices during the currency of the contract is worked out:

options.A: As per the rates demanded by the supplier from time to time
options.B: Only on the basis of the consumer price index, in all contracts
options.C: At the discretion of the depot officer
options.D: With reference to the indices and the formula stipulated in the contract

e: Under the price variation clause, adjustment of prices during the currency of the contract is worked out with reference to the indices and the formula stipulated in the contract.

q: In the e-auction of scrap, the 'reserve price' (upset price) of a lot is:

options.A: The minimum price fixed before the auction, below which the lot is ordinarily not sold without the approval of the competent authority
options.B: The highest price ever received for a similar lot in the past
options.C: The price quoted by the first bidder in the auction
options.D: The book value of the lot plus the ground rent

e: The reserve price (upset price) of a scrap lot is the minimum price fixed before the auction, below which the lot is ordinarily not sold without the approval of the competent authority.

q:
Consider the following statements about the e-auction of scrap:
1. Scrap lots are sold on an 'as is where is' basis, the purchaser taking the material in its existing condition and position.
2. Intending bidders are given an opportunity to inspect the lots before the auction.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: scrap lots are sold on an 'as is where is' basis, the purchaser taking the material in its existing condition and position, and intending bidders are given an opportunity to inspect the lots beforehand.

q: The earnest money deposited by the successful bidder in an e-auction of scrap is:

options.A: Refunded to him immediately after the auction in all cases
options.B: Adjusted towards the sale value payable by him for the lot
options.C: Forfeited to the Railway in all cases
options.D: Credited to the Stock Adjustment Account

e: The earnest money deposited by the successful bidder in a scrap e-auction is adjusted towards the sale value payable by him for the lot.
